senses.gloss: m. (χρυσοάργυρον, usu. χρυσάργυρον) gold and silver tax levied by Constantine the Great (v. Sachs Beitr. II, 140; Rapap. Er. Mill. p. 193, a. authors there quoted).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 3:1:4">Y. B. Kam. III, 3ᶜ</cite> top <he>אהן כ׳ א׳ וכ׳</he> as to the chrysargyron: before that tax is arranged, it is permitted to say (to the officers), ‘this man is my fellow-trader’; when it has been arranged (and is being collected), it is not permitted (because it would injure the person omitted in the list without alleviating the burden of others); cmp. <cite ref="A01741"><he>אכסניי</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>כְּרִיסַרְגּוּרִיּוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:2">Cant. R. II, 2</cite> (variously corrupted).—

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 12">Midr. Till. to Ps. XII</cite> <cite ref="M02513"><he>מרגזאות</he></cite>, ed. Bub. <he>מזה נמסאות</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 656">Yalk. ib. 656</cite> <he>מדגראות</he>, read: <he>כְּרִיזַרְגְּרָאוֹת</he> (ascribed to Hadrian).
